selection_reason: Uncontrolled title value -> unquoted HTML attribute injection -> potential XSS via attribute breakouts
source_summary: title parameter comes directly from marked.js parser, which parses markdown link syntax [text](href "title") where title is user-controlled markdown content
sink_summary: HTML title attribute rendered without quotes into document.innerHTML, allowing attribute breakout and script injection
guard_summary: Only href is sanitized against javascript: and vbscript: protocols when this.options.sanitize is true. Title parameter receives no validation, sanitization, or HTML escaping. The sanitize option is not explicitly passed to marked() in render().
risk_pattern: Unquoted HTML attribute injection: user-controlled title value inserted without quotes into title attribute, allowing injection of additional attributes and JavaScript via whitespace and special characters
enclosing_conditions: href protocol checks for javascript: and vbscript:
context_summary: Custom markdown renderer for Electron app that converts markdown links to HTML anchors. The title attribute is rendered without quotes while href receives some protocol validation when sanitize option is enabled.
unresolved_facts: Whether this.options.sanitize is ever set to true in practice
How marked.js parses and normalizes the title parameter from markdown input
Whether the Electron context provides any additional HTML sanitization

cwe_assessments.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-77 specifically addresses command injection where input modifies OS/shell commands. The demonstrated behavior is HTML attribute injection into DOM, not command construction or execution.

connection.evidence: User-controlled title parameter from markdown input flows directly into unquoted HTML attribute construction via string interpolation

diff_causality.evidence: The added line introduces the unquoted title attribute insertion. Reverting would remove this injection point.

security_control.required_control: HTML attribute quoting and content sanitization
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: Unquoted attributes require validation to prevent attribute breakout
existing_controls_checked: href protocol validation when sanitize option enabled
no title validation or escaping observed
security_control.deficiency_evidence: Title parameter receives no validation, sanitization, or proper HTML attribute quoting

concrete_impact.evidence: Unquoted attribute could allow attribute breakout and script injection in browser context, but specific exploit path through Electron's security model is not demonstrated

cwe_assessments.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered at all, eliminating the unquoted attribute injection vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled title parameter flows directly into unquoted HTML attribute
No validation or escaping applied to title parameter before HTML construction
contradicting_evidence: CWE-77 requires command construction/execution mechanism, demonstrated behavior is HTML/DOM injection
No shell command construction or execution observed in the code path
unresolved_facts: Whether this.options.sanitize is enabled in practice
Electron's specific security context and Content Security Policy
How marked.js normalizes title parameter from markdown input

cwe_assessments.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-93 specifically addresses CRLF sequence injection for protocol/format manipulation, not HTML attribute injection. The demonstrated vulnerability involves unquoted HTML attribute injection, not CRLF-based protocol injection.

connection.evidence: User-controlled title parameter from markdown input flows directly into unquoted HTML title attribute via string interpolation: `title=${title}`

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered at all when title is null, preventing the injection vector. The addition creates the vulnerable code path.

security_control.required_control: CRLF sequence neutralization for protocol/format boundaries
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-93 requires controls specifically for CRLF sequence neutralization in protocol contexts
existing_controls_checked: No CRLF-specific validation observed in the code path
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The demonstrated issue is HTML attribute quoting deficiency, not CRLF injection. No evidence shows CRLF sequences being used as special elements or requiring neutralization.

concrete_impact.evidence: Unquoted attribute allows injection of additional HTML attributes and JavaScript via whitespace characters, enabling XSS in the Electron application context

cwe_assessments.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered when title is null, eliminating the unquoted attribute injection vector entirely.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled title parameter flows directly into unquoted HTML attribute
No validation or escaping applied to title parameter before HTML construction
contradicting_evidence: CWE-93 mechanism focuses on CRLF sequence injection for protocols/formats, not HTML attribute injection
No evidence of CRLF sequences being used as special separators in this context
unresolved_facts: Whether this.options.sanitize is enabled in practice
How marked.js normalizes title parameter parsing

cwe_assessments.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-1321 specifically involves modifying JavaScript object prototypes through property assignment. The demonstrated behavior is HTML attribute injection, not prototype pollution.

connection.evidence: User-controlled title parameter flows to HTML construction, but this is DOM manipulation, not JavaScript object prototype modification.

diff_causality.evidence: The added line creates an HTML injection vulnerability by rendering title attribute without quotes, but this doesn't relate to object prototype modification.

security_control.required_control: Input validation and sanitization for object property assignments
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-1321 requires controls to prevent unauthorized modification of object prototype attributes
existing_controls_checked: No object property assignment validation observed
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The demonstrated code performs HTML construction, not object property assignment, so the CWE-1321 control requirement is irrelevant to the actual vulnerability

concrete_impact.evidence: The demonstrated impact is HTML injection/XSS, not prototype pollution which would affect JavaScript object inheritance chains.

cwe_assessments.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the title attribute would still be unquoted but the vulnerability would remain HTML injection, not prototype pollution.
contradicting_evidence: CWE-1321 involves JavaScript object prototype modification, but the code performs HTML DOM construction
The vulnerability mechanism is unquoted HTML attribute injection, not property assignment to object prototypes
The impact is client-side XSS, not server-side prototype pollution affecting object inheritance
unresolved_facts: Whether this code ever handles JavaScript object property assignment
Whether prototype pollution vectors exist elsewhere in the application
